Which kind of commercial oven do you need?

Caterkwik sell 442 ovens across 23 types. Almost everyone starts in the same place: a burner range, sized by how many covers leave the pass at your busiest service.

If you bake, you want a convection oven rather than a static one. If you have no gas, electric and induction cover the same jobs. If the menu is the point — tandoor, charcoal, wood, rotisserie — those are their own types below.

Pick what you cook, what supply you have and how busy you get, and the page narrows to the types that fit.

Questions their sales line takes every day

Which oven does a pub or cafe kitchen need?

Almost always a burner range. Caterkwik's 4 Burner Ovens start at £1,337.99 ex VAT and suit a tight run with moderate covers; move to a 6 Burner once you are past about eighty covers a service; they start at £1,132.99, lower than the 4 Burner, because the entry-level Lincat Silverlink sits in that category. With no gas supply, an Electric Range does the same job from £921.99.

Gas or electric?

Whatever the building has. Eleven of the twenty-three types run on mains gas or bottled LPG, eleven on electricity, and three burn wood or charcoal. The catch with electric is supply: most commercial electric ovens want three phase, so check the board before you fall for one. Pick your supply in the finder above and the types that will not run on it disappear.

What is the difference between a static oven and a convection oven?

A static oven heats from an element or a burner underneath, so the bottom shelf runs hotter than the top. A convection oven has a fan that moves the air, so every shelf bakes the same. For roasting and general service static is fine; for pastry, bread and anything in batches on trays you want convection. Caterkwik stock 135 electric convection ovens from £229.99 and 12 gas ones from £3,249.99.

What is a cook and hold oven for?

Cooking joints slowly overnight at a low temperature, then holding them at serving temperature until they are needed. Less shrinkage, less labour in the morning, and the oven is working while the kitchen is empty. 15 models, from £1,379.99 ex VAT, all electric.

Do you sell ovens for pizza, tandoori or charcoal cooking?

Yes, each is its own type. Wood Fired Ovens for pizza and bread from £6,039.00, 25 Charcoal Ovens from £2,169.99, and two Tandoori Ovens, one gas and one charcoal, both priced on application. Gas deck pizza ovens are in the separate Pizza Ovens category on caterkwik.co.uk.

Why do some types say none available?

Because that is what their catalogue holds today. Domestic Ovens lists two models and both are discontinued; Tandoori Ovens lists two and both are price on application. The page shows the count rather than hiding the type, so nobody clicks through to an empty shelf.
